newsitem.title: USA: Calif.'s unemployment rate drops to 6.5 pct-state.
newsitem.headline: Calif.'s unemployment rate drops to 6.5 pct-state.

text.p: California's unemployment rate dropped sharply to 6.5 percent in February, down from a revised 6.9 percent in January, state officials reported on Friday.
The February rate was the lowest unemployment rate in the state since October 1990, the state's Employment Development Department said. The unemployment rate in February 1996 was 7.6 percent.
The number of people employed in California was 14,746,000 in February, an increase of 59,000 over the month and up 401,000 compared with February 1996, the department said.
The number of unemployed continued to decline, down 60,000 over the month and down 154,000 over the year. The number of unemployed in February was 1,024,000, the department said.
California Gov. Pete Wilson hailed February's figures.

"Today's good news on the employment front reaffirms the effects of our efforts to make California golden once again," Wilson, a Republican, said. He said recent tax cuts and the repeal of regulations had bolstered the state's economy.
All industry divisions, except one, posted job gains over the month, the Employment Development Department reported.

Employment in retail trade showed the largest growth, up 12,400 jobs over the month. Strong employment gains were also recorded over the month in construction, up 10,200 jobs and services, up 6,300 jobs, the department said.
The job loss by the finance, insurance and real estate sector amounted to only 100 jobs, the department said.
